propositions: Multiple git bundles for a single ref cause clone hard-failure ('multiple updates for ref not allowed') and stall push operations when helper rejects ('multiple bundles exists on server'); events divergent between heads are irretrievably lost when upstream's interactive Doctor discards the non-chosen head

Rebar must autonomously heal multi-bundle divergence via lossless iterated 2-parent merges (reusing sync's _union_merge semantics), never discarding a head, by folding divergent bundle tips under rebar's write_lock and git-remote-s3's S3 per-ref lock with write-then-delete crash-safe ordering
The doctor must detect the multi-bundle condition from stderr signatures and auto-invoke once per push attempt with a healed_once guard, retrying the push after collapsing to a single merged bundle

The heal acquires the helper's conditional-put S3 lock, re-enumerates bundles under lock (TOCTOU guard), fetches all heads locally into scratch refs, folds them via iterated 2-parent git merges with --allow-unrelated-histories support, writes the merged tip as a new bundle object before any deletes, deletes originals without deleting the merged tip, and releases the lock, ensuring at least one lossless bundle exists at every crash point

On a genuine content conflict in a non-derived file the heal aborts without deleting remote bundles, releases the lock, and surfaces fsck-recover; concurrent doctors back off when the S3 lock is held, letting the lock-holder's merge collapse the shared remote for all processes

The heal operates entirely through git-remote-s3's existing public API (S3Remote, acquire_lock/release_lock, get_bundles_for_ref, .s3 client for put_object/delete_object) with lazy import behind require_s3_helper(), adding no direct boto3 dependency to core rebar since boto3 ships transitively under the [s3] extra
